title: collect function runs commands without per-item timeouts in the loop

finding.claim: collect function runs commands without per-item timeouts in the loop
finding.recommendation: Pass a per-command timeout from the config or a default and enforce it in _execute, or add a timeout wrapper around the subprocess.Popen call to prevent a single hung command from exhausting resources across all items.

code_region.text:
items = []

    sandbox_root = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="codereview-evidence-")
    workdir = os.path.join(sandbox_root, "tree")
    try:
        try:
            _copy_tree(source_dir, workdir)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            for entry in config.get("commands") or []:
                items.append(_result(
                    str(entry.get("name") or entry.get("command")),
                    "command", entry.get("required", True), "error",
                    None, 0.0, b"",
                    detail=f"sandbox copy failed: {exc}",
                    command=str(entry.get("command"))))
            for entry in config.get("adapters") or []:
                items.append(_result(
                    str(entry.get("name")), "adapter",
                    entry.get("required", False), "error", None, 0.0,
                    b"", detail=f"sandbox copy failed: {exc}"))
            return _record(config, source_dir, items,

refutation.reason: The loop does assign a per-item timeout from each command entry, falling back to the configured default. That timeout is then passed into _execute for enforcement, so the claim that commands run without per-item timeouts is incorrect.

probe.summary: Evidence-timeout probe (`probes/closingB_evidence.py`, 8f77565b56a4 section): a `sleep 10` command was run through evidence collection with per-item timeout=1. Result: status='timeout' after 1.0s (recorded duration_s=1.005) — the per-item timeout at evidence.py:407 IS enforced by _execute (evidence.py:268-301), contrary to the claim's reading of the call.
